meta.title: Health Tech Product Manager Roadmap
meta.shortDescription: Operate as the strategic bridge between clinician and patient users, business objectives, and engineering teams, directing what gets built, for whom, and why.
meta.bestFor: Clinicians who constantly questioned system design, designed workarounds, and thought deeply about user needs and trade-offs.

roleSnapshot.oneLiner: Health Tech Product Managers operate as the strategic bridge between clinician and patient users, business objectives, and engineering teams, directing what gets built, for whom, and why.
roleSnapshot.bestSuitedFor: The clinician who constantly said 'why does this system make my job harder?' and then designed workarounds for their entire unit. The pharmacist who redesigned the medication reconciliation process before anyone asked. Anyone who naturally thinks in systems, trade-offs, and user needs.
roleSnapshot.workSetting: Predominantly remote or hybrid. 29% of tech PM roles are hybrid, 13% fully remote. Health tech companies lead adoption of remote work compared to traditional healthcare organizations.
roleSnapshot.demandSignal: Strong growth. 6,000+ PM positions currently open, 53.6% above 2023 lows, with 40 to 50% growth in product hiring year-over-year. Senior PM roles show 87% year-on-year growth. Health tech is among the highest-compensating sectors for PMs.
roleSnapshot.keyDifferentiator: This is the longest but most rewarding transition path (6 to 12 months vs. 3 to 6 for analyst roles). PM demands business strategy, user research methodology, technical communication, and stakeholder management on top of healthcare domain knowledge. However, it offers the highest visibility and leadership ceiling of any role in this collection.
whereTheyWork: Digital health startups (Hinge Health, Luro Health)
Health insurance and payer tech (CVS Health, GoodRx)
clinicalAdvantage: You understand user needs from lived clinical experience
You recognize what features will actually get used in practice
You understand compliance and regulatory constraints naturally
You evaluate products through clinical lens, not just business metrics
You navigate stakeholder complexity across clinical departments

nurses.tech: User research prioritization: structuring interviews, identifying which user segments have most critical pain points, prioritizing which problems product should solve first
nurses.explanation: Your triage skills apply directly to user research and problem prioritization

nurses.tech: Stakeholder management: coordinating between engineering, design, clinical advisors, sales, legal while ensuring alignment through shared documentation
nurses.explanation: Your coordination skills translate directly to cross-functional product leadership

nurses.tech: Product process improvement: mapping current state workflows, identifying friction, designing features that eliminate bottlenecks
nurses.explanation: You already think about efficiency and user experience

nurses.tech: Data-driven decision making: reading A/B test results, funnel analysis, cohort retention data, distinguishing signal from noise
nurses.explanation: Your evidence evaluation translates to analytics interpretation

nurses.tech: User-centric product advocacy: pushing back on engineering estimates that create poor UX, questioning design decisions that ignore user research
nurses.explanation: Your safety advocacy becomes product advocacy

pharmacists.tech: Product requirements definition: evaluating appropriateness by considering diagnosis, comorbidities, contraindications, outcomes translates directly to writing PRDs with success criteria
pharmacists.explanation: Your MTM thinking applies to feature specification

pharmacists.clinical: Drug information research and clinical literature review
pharmacists.tech: Competitive analysis and market research: synthesizing evidence on drugs becomes synthesizing competitor products and market trends
pharmacists.explanation: Your research skills apply to competitive intelligence

pharmacists.tech: User adoption strategy: counseling patients on adherence translates to designing for behavior change, not just functionality
pharmacists.explanation: You understand what drives user behavior change

pharmacists.tech: Product operations and prioritization: managing drug availability and cost optimization becomes resource allocation and roadmap prioritization
pharmacists.explanation: Your supply chain thinking applies to product prioritization

pharmacists.tech: Healthcare regulatory product development: understanding FDA regulations and insurance rules means fluently knowing what is legally possible in product decisions
pharmacists.explanation: Your regulatory knowledge is a direct advantage

otherClinicians.tech: Problem definition: systematic evidence evaluation becomes user research, root cause analysis, scoping product requirements
otherClinicians.explanation: Your diagnostic thinking applies to problem definition

otherClinicians.tech: Product roadmap and strategy: creating individualized treatment plans considering patient goals becomes creating product roadmaps considering user goals and business constraints
otherClinicians.explanation: Your planning skills scale to product strategy

otherClinicians.tech: KPI definition and success metrics: tracking healing time and functional improvement becomes defining retention, engagement, clinical efficiency metrics
otherClinicians.explanation: Your outcomes thinking applies to product metrics

otherClinicians.tech: Cross-functional product leadership: translating medical complexity to non-medical audiences becomes translating technical complexity to non-technical stakeholders
otherClinicians.explanation: You already navigate complex stakeholder groups

otherClinicians.tech: Strategic learning and competitive intelligence: staying current on healthcare policy, competitor moves, technology trends
otherClinicians.explanation: You already synthesize complex information systematically

phases.name: Foundation
topics: PM Fundamentals: vision, strategy, roadmap, user research, prioritization frameworks
Product Frameworks: Jobs to Be Done (JTBD), user personas, problem statements
Health Tech Market Landscape: types of companies, regulatory environment (HIPAA, FDA), key stakeholders
Basic Technical Literacy: APIs, EHRs, data flow, system integration concepts

resources.name: Lenny Rachitsky Newsletter Start Here collection
Maven: Technical Foundations for Product Managers
resources.description: Free 8-day email course on technical literacy

phases.checkpoint: Write a 1 to 2 page Health Tech Market Overview identifying 3 companies, their products, customers, and PM challenges.

phases.name: Technical Depth
topics: User Research: interviews, journey mapping, persona development, research synthesis
Data Analytics for PMs: metrics, funnels, A/B testing, cohort analysis
Product Frameworks: OKRs, product strategy, competitive analysis, pricing models
Agile and Scrum: sprints, backlogs, estimation, retrospectives, PM role in Agile
PRD Writing and Product Requirements Definition
Wireframing Basics: low-fidelity prototyping, understanding UX

resources.name: API Fundamentals for Product Managers on Maven

phases.checkpoint: Conduct 5+ user interviews with clinicians. Write research synthesis. Create competitive analysis of 3 health tech products. Write a PRD for a hypothetical feature.

phases.name: Specialization
topics: Track A: Clinical Workflow Products (EHR features, provider-facing tools)
Track B: Patient-Facing Digital Health Apps (portals, remote monitoring, engagement)
Track C: Population Health and Care Coordination Platforms
Track D: Regulatory and Compliance-Focused Products
Track E: Pharmacy and Medication Technology

resources.name: Specialization research and case studies
resources.description: Deep dives in chosen specialization area

phases.checkpoint: 4 to 6 page product strategy case study demonstrating clinical domain expertise applied to chosen specialization.

certifications.realityCheck: Product management hiring is heavily portfolio and experience-driven, NOT certification-driven. Job postings emphasize 'demonstrated PM experience' and 'ability to ship products,' not credentials.

items.name: Certified Scrum Product Owner (CSPO)
items.timeline: 15 to 20% of health tech PM postings
items.notes: Useful if working in Scrum-heavy organizations but not required

items.name: SAFe Product Owner and Product Manager (SAFe POPM)
items.notes: Common in larger organizations with SAFe framework

items.name: Reforge Courses
items.timeline: No credential but widely respected by hiring managers
items.notes: Portfolio-heavy and highly valued in tech industry

items.name: Product School or General Assembly Bootcamp
items.timeline: 5 to 10% of postings mention PM training
items.notes: Can help if you have no prior product experience but expensive

items.name: Health Informatics Masters
items.timeline: Appears in some advanced PM postings

items.name: CCRPS (Clinical Research Project Manager)
items.timeline: Only relevant for clinical trial products
items.notes: Specialty credential for clinical research focus

items.name: AIPMM Certified Product Manager
items.timeline: Less than 2% of PM job postings

items.name: Data science certifications
items.timeline: Only relevant for analytics-heavy PM roles
items.notes: Wrong skill set for product management

items.name: Generic PM certifications from unknown providers

certifications.recommendation: Skip certifications initially. Invest in Reforge courses and portfolio projects before any certification. 'Show me your portfolio. Show me products you have built. Show me the impact you had.' Certifications are differentiators, not requirements.

portfolioProjects.title: Clinical Workflow Optimization PRD
portfolioProjects.description: Interview 5+ nurses and pharmacists about medication reconciliation, map current workflow, identify friction, propose EHR feature with wireframe and success metrics.
portfolioProjects.clinicalAdvantage: You know the actual workflow including workarounds, not the theoretical one

portfolioProjects.title: Patient Engagement Strategy
portfolioProjects.description: Conduct user interviews with patients on chronic disease management, analyze competitor engagement features, propose 2 to 3 engagement features with wireframes.
portfolioProjects.clinicalAdvantage: You understand patient behavior change and what motivates adherence

portfolioProjects.title: Pharmacy Technology Feature Strategy
portfolioProjects.description: Map pharmacist MTM workflow end-to-end, identify time waste, propose software redesign with wireframes and business impact (especially for pharmacists).
portfolioProjects.clinicalAdvantage: You have lived the MTM workflow and know where real bottlenecks are

portfolioProjects.title: Competitive Market Strategy
portfolioProjects.description: Analyze 4 to 5 competitors, conduct user research, identify white space, propose prioritized 12-month roadmap.
portfolioProjects.clinicalAdvantage: You evaluate telehealth through clinical lens, not just business metrics

portfolioProjects.title: Regulatory Compliance PRD
portfolioProjects.description: Analyze regulatory requirements, assess current gaps, write PRD for HIPAA audit log feature or clinical data privacy with wireframes and rollout strategy.
portfolioProjects.clinicalAdvantage: You understand compliance from the frontline, not just the legal department

verified.name: June Srisethnil, DPT
verified.summary: Physical therapist to clinical product manager. Transition took approximately 7 years. Moved from clinical practice to clinical sales (transition role), then self-taught PM skills via Udemy and LinkedIn Learning before joining health tech startup.

transitionStories.note: Published first-person transition stories from clinicians with the exact title 'Product Manager' at health tech companies are sparse. This is partly because PM transitions happen through internal moves and startup hiring that are rarely documented publicly. However, multiple health tech companies (Teladoc, Ro, Hinge Health, Epic, athenahealth) explicitly welcome and hire clinicians into PM roles. Active crowdsourcing needed, especially for nurse and pharmacist transitions.

firstThreeMoves.title: Map your clinical assets
firstThreeMoves.description: Identify clinical workflows you deeply understand and potential product applications.
specifics: Write a 1-page document identifying which clinical workflows you deeply understand
Note what frustrated you most about them
Identify which health tech products touch those workflows
Describe how you would have designed them differently

firstThreeMoves.title: Conduct one user research interview
firstThreeMoves.description: Practice user research by conducting a real interview.
specifics: Conduct 30 to 45 minute Jobs to Be Done interview about a workflow or product they use
Document what you learned and what surprised you
This starts building your research muscle and generates data for portfolio projects

firstThreeMoves.title: Start PM foundations learning
specifics: Subscribe to Lenny Rachitsky's Newsletter and read the Start Here collection (free)
OR enroll in Maven's Technical Foundations for Product Managers (free 8-day email course)
OR research the next Reforge cohort start date
